'''''Sedum pachyphyllum''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the stonecrop family, [[Crassulaceae]].<ref name="POWO">{{Cite web |title=Sedum pachyphyllum Rose {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:231817-2 |access-date=2025-11-07 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Sedum pachyphyllum'' is a [[Succulent plant|succulent]] [[perennial]] growing {{cvt|10–30|cm|0}} tall from a woody base. Its stems are branched and can either stand erect or spread across the ground. The [[glaucous]] leaves are {{cvt|3–4|cm}} long with circular cross sections {{cvt|8–10|mm|1}} wide and grow perpendicularly from the stems.<ref name="Rose-1911">{{Cite journal |last=Rose |first=J. N. |date=1911 |title=STUDIES OF MEXICAN AND CENTRAL AMERICAN PLANTS—No. 7 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23491875 |journal=Contributions from the United States National Herbarium |volume=13 |issue=9 |pages=I–X |jstor=23491875 |issn=0097-1618}}</ref> In dry conditions, the tips of the leaves become reddish.<ref name="Stillwell-1975">{{Cite journal |last=Stillwell |first=M. |date=1975 |title=Cultivation of Succulents |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/42786071 |journal=The Cactus and Succulent Journal of Great Britain |volume=37 |issue=1 |pages=8–9 |jstor=42786071 |issn=0007-9375}}</ref>

The flowering stem is {{cvt|2|cm|1}} long, spreading laterally, with flowers attached by short [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]]. The flowers have 5 green [[sepal]]s, about {{cvt|6|mm}} long and widely spreading; [[petal]]s are yellow and {{cvt|7|mm}} long. The [[Type (biology)|type specimen]] was observed blooming in January.<ref name="Rose-1911" />

== Distribution ==
''Sedum pachyphyllum'' is [[Endemism|endemic]] to central [[Mexico]], where it grows in the [[Sierra Mixteca]].<ref name="POWO" /><ref name="auto">{{Cite journal |last=Uhl |first=Charles H. |date=1978 |title=Chromosomes of Mexican Sedum Ii. Section Pachysedum |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23311260 |journal=Rhodora |volume=80 |issue=824 |pages=491–512 |jstor=23311260 |issn=0035-4902}}</ref> Because of its use as an ornamental plant, ''S. pachyphyllum'' has become established outside its native range, especially in Spain, where [[Naturalized species|naturalized]] populations have been documented in the provinces of [[Province of Valencia|Valencia]] and [[Province of Castellón|Castellón]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Senar |first1=R. |last2=Cardero |first2=S. |date=2019 |title=Dades de plantes al·lòctones per a l'est de la península Ibèrica / Data of alien plants for the east of the Iberian Peninsula |url=https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/03b5/41a2ceb5bbab3a4164414964ef6b5e07285e.pdf |journal=Collectanea Botanica |volume=38 |issue= |pages=e009 |doi=10.3989/collectbot.2019.v38.009 |access-date=2025-11-06}}</ref> In Italy, a naturalized population of plants growing near [[Riva del Garda]] were identified as hybrids between ''S. pachyphyllum'' and ''Echeveria agavoides''.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gallo |first1=Lorenzo |last2=Merli |first2=Marco |last3=Jankalski |first3=Stephen |date=2020-06-26 |title=×Sedeveria mauroi (Crassulaceae), a new alien species established in NE Italy |url=https://bioone.org/journals/bradleya/volume-2020/issue-38/brad.n38.2020.a19/Sedeveria-mauroi-Crassulaceae-a-new-alien-species-established-in-NE/10.25223/brad.n38.2020.a19.full |journal=Bradleya |volume=2020 |issue=38 |pages=187 |doi=10.25223/brad.n38.2020.a19 |bibcode=2020Bradl2020..187G |issn=0265-086X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
The [[Type (biology)|type specimen]] of ''Sedum pachyphyllum'' was collected by Carl Albert Purpus in 1907 near [[San Luis Amatlán]] in [[Oaxaca]].<ref name="Rose-1911" /> [[Joseph Nelson Rose]] formally described the species in 1911. Its species epithet, ''pachyphyllum'', comes from the Greek words ''pachys'' (meaning thick) and ''phyton'' (meaning plant), referring to the plant's thick, fleshy leaves.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bayton |first=Ross |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctvvh85k9 |title=The Gardener's Botanical: An Encyclopedia of Latin Plant Names - with More than 5,000 Entries |date=2020 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-20017-0 |pages=223 |doi=10.2307/j.ctvvh85k9 |jstor=j.ctvvh85k9 }}</ref> ''S. pachyphyllum'' belongs to a [[clade]] of about 90 closely-related species within the ''Sedum'' genus called section ''Pachysedum'', one of 22 sections named by [[Alwin Berger]] in 1930.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite book |last=Berger |first=Alwin |title=Crassulaceae |publisher=Verlag von Wilhelm Engelmann |year=1930 |editor1-last=Engler |editor1-first=Adolf |series=Die Natürlichen Pflanzenfamilien |volume=18A |location=Leipzig |pages=352–483 |editor2-last=Prantl |editor2-first=Karl Anton}}</ref>

Two [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrids]] with ''S. pachyphyllum'' parentage have been formally described. The artificial hybrid [[Sedum rubrotinctum|''Sedum'' × ''rubrotinctum'']] (''S. pachyphyllum'' × ''S. stahlii''), sometimes called the jelly bean plant, is a popular [[ornamental plant]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sedum × rubrotinctum R.T.Clausen {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:275989-1 |access-date=2025-11-07 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> The intergeneric hybrid × ''Sedeveria mauroi'' (''Echeveria agavoides'' × ''S. pachyphyllum'') is an [[introduced species]] in Italy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=× Sedeveria mauroi L.Gallo, Merli & Jankalski {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77211398-1 |access-date=2025-11-07 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

== Uses ==
''Sedum pachyphyllum'' is cultivated, including for use in gardens and on [[green roof]]s, in part because of its [[drought tolerance]].<ref name="Stillwell-1975" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Farrell |first1=Claire |last2=Szota |first2=Christopher |last3=Williams |first3=Nicholas S. G. |last4=Arndt |first4=Stefan K. |date=2013 |title=High water users can be drought tolerant: using physiological traits for green roof plant selection |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/42953056 |journal=Plant and Soil |volume=372 |issue=1/2 |pages=177–193 |doi=10.1007/s11104-013-1725-x |jstor=42953056 |bibcode=2013PlSoi.372..177F |issn=0032-079X}}</ref>
